sections.intro: All tempo reps are 100m at roughly 70 percent, controlled and relaxed.
items: Weeks 1–2: 2 sets of 6 reps. Jog 50m and walk 50m between reps. Rest 3 minutes between sets.
Weeks 3–4: 2 sets of 8 to 10 reps. Rest 30 seconds between reps and 3 minutes between sets.
Weeks 5–6: Mixed sets, finishing with a 250m rep in the final session each week.
sections.title: Tempo progression

items: Weeks 1–2: 3 x 8 at a weight that leaves 3 good reps in reserve.
Weeks 3–4: 3 x 8. Add load where week 2 felt clean.
Weeks 5–6: 4 x 6, heavier. Add one rep per set on single-leg work.
Nordic curls stay eccentric-only for the whole program: 2 x 4 with a 4-second lower, band-assisted as needed.

retest.title: Lab Retest

items: Week 1: Pogo hops and low box jumps. Landings come first.
Week 2: Countermovement jumps and broad jumps, 4 x 4.
Week 3: Single-leg hops to a stick landing, kept at low volume.
Week 4: Depth landings from a low box into an immediate jump, 3 x 3. Use this only when the athlete landed cleanly through weeks 1–3.
sections.title: Plyometric progression

sections.intro: The timing rule for every First Step session.
items: Time the Day 1 starts every week. Phone timing is fine. Use timing gates when they are available.
Log the times in the app with the session. The Day 1 starts are timed over 10m and 30m, and both are tests in the catalog, so the times are logged in Testing and show in the Speed Report.
If times fall off by more than a few percent inside a session, the session ends.
Speed work stops when it stops being speed work.
sections.title: The Lab Standard

subtitle: For the athlete whose sport is won in the first 10 metres
summary: Three sessions a week built around acceleration and power. Every session starts fast while the athlete is fresh, and every week is timed.

details: Falling starts and 3-point starts: 8 to 10 reps over 10m
Use full recovery, about 1 minute per rep
